initial.title: [v0.92][migration] Migrate pre-topology bound issue records to Git topology
initial.goal: Migrate every pre-#5886 bound record with incomplete topology into truthful current C-SDLC v2 state.
initial.required_outcome: All affected records receive a deterministic disposition and open never-bound issues become normally bindable without restoring claims.
declared_scope: One typed migration operation under the current csdlc-issue owner
Per-issue disposition evidence and focused regression tests
authority_boundary: Canonical .csdlc issue records and verified Git worktree topology
Explicit live GitHub issue-state snapshot supplied as typed input
operator_constraints: Treat this as state migration, not tooling reliability work
Do not restore claims, leases, heartbeats, or preparation state
Do not hand-edit canonical issue records
initial.task_boundary: Implement and prove one deterministic migration for records rendered bound without topology before the #5886 cutover.
deliverables: Typed migration request and result contracts
Focused migration tests and cohort disposition evidence
acceptance_criteria: The exact affected cohort is inventoried before mutation
Every record is classified using canonical state, live issue state, and actual Git topology
Open never-bound records become initialized and normally bindable
Verified existing topology and terminal records are preserved truthfully
Cards, authored artifacts, audit history, identity, and digest integrity are preserved
Ambiguous topology and digest mismatch fail before mutation
The operation is idempotent and emits a per-issue disposition report
Doctor no longer rejects migrated records solely for bound null topology
Issue 5844 becomes bindable through current csdlc-bind
Focused tests cover all required positive and negative classifications
non_goals: Restoring removed claim or preparation authority
Binding or implementing migrated product issues
initial.plan_summary: Define typed migration contracts, classify the full cohort before writes, atomically reset only unambiguous open never-bound records, prove idempotence and negative cases, then validate the real cohort and WP-24 bindability.

steps.action: Implement typed request, disposition, report, and dry-run classification for the exact legacy shape.
Apply atomic record migration only after full classification succeeds, preserving cards and audit truth.
Add focused tests for all positive, negative, and idempotent cases.
Run the real cohort migration, retain dispositions, and prove current doctor plus WP-24 bindability.

invariants: Git branch/worktree topology remains the sole binding authority
No record changes before complete classification succeeds
No branch or worktree value is invented
Terminal truth and retained evidence are immutable
A second migration pass makes no changes
risks: A historical branch name may resemble issue topology without being authoritative
A partial migration could strand records unless classification is transaction-wide
Closed records may require preservation rather than phase reset
stop_conditions: Any record or card digest fails verification
Live topology is ambiguous or only partially matches
Live issue state is missing for a cohort member
The migration would alter cards, authored evidence, or terminal truth

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove classification, atomicity, preservation, failure behavior, and idempotence through focused Rust tests.
Prove the exact before and after cohort counts, dispositions, second-run no-op, current doctor results, and issue 5844 bindability.
validation_lanes.defer_reason: Validator is produced with the implementation and runs against the final migrated cohort.

validation_lanes.proof_role: Reject whitespace errors in migration code, tests, records, and evidence.

initial.failure_policy: Fail before any mutation on invalid digest, missing issue state, ambiguous topology, partial topology, or classification error; retain a complete diagnostic report.
review_prompts: Can any classification invent topology, reopen terminal work, or reset a genuinely bound issue?
Does any failure permit partial cohort mutation?
Are cards, authored evidence, audit history, and digests preserved?
Is the second run demonstrably a no-op?
Does the design retain #5886 topology authority without restoring claims?
initial.review_scope: Issue 5896 typed migration contracts, current v2 migration implementation, focused tests, the exact cohort disposition, and WP-24 bindability proof.
